models: deepseek-v4.1-flash via OpenCode Go (opencode run --pure, tool-less agent)
summary: First phase on 156 HumanEval problems, one model, 3 repetitions, up to 5 rounds with visible-only feedback. Aleph with llms.txt reaches 85.0% pass@1 against 99.4% for Python and 96.8% against 98.3% after feedback, but spends about 8x the tokens per solved problem (median session 7.7k vs 0.5k tokens), mostly reasoning tokens and the llms.txt spec; written code is about the same size.

hypotheses.note: pass@1 gap -14.3 points, 95% CI [-18.6, -10.5]; after up to 5 rounds the gap is -1.5 points [-2.6, -0.6].
tokens per solved problem 13.2k vs 1.6k, ratio 8.4 [4.9, 16.1]; medians per session: reasoning 3808 vs 121, net input 3283 vs 158 (llms.txt), output 228 vs 185.
reasoning text was not captured, only its token count; the reasoning gap (31x median) is compatible with translation or with working out an unfamiliar language.
not measured: HumanEval problems do no file access.
